preamble: Voicing of the alveolar ejective [tʼ] to [d]. Proto-Nakh ejectives (Nikolayev & Starostin 1994; Nichols 2003; Schrijver 2021) are kept in Bats (Tsova-Tush), the most conservative Nakh language. In Chechen and Ingush (Vainakh), single non-initial ejectives after a vowel or sonorant became voiced, while word-initial ejectives and *qʼ survive; geminate ejectives and ejectives after x instead lost glottalization but stayed voiceless. Initial ejectives are untouched even in the same word (*ṗHenṭo 'rib' > Chechen пӏенда pʼenda), showing a lenition of non-initial ejectives. A minority view (Deseriev, Imnaishvili) took the Bats ejectives as secondary, but all current reconstructions treat them as original (Fallon 2002).

examples.note: Bats pʼʕentʼo; the initial pʼ stays ejective.
